answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because vertex only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, willow is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any voyage approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
